This Dar was filed on 26.04.2022 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of
the parties which was registere
. The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 15.10.2021 in which one Smt. Sunita Pal D/o Sh.Rakeshwar Pal (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per petitioner, on 15.10.2021, she alongwith her two brothers Sh.
Manish Pal and Sh. Nitesh Pal was travelling from Chandigarh to Delhi to visit her uncle's house.
They were walking on footpath near Shastri Nagar Metro Station, heading towards Pratap Nagar Metro Station.

Her brothers were walking ahead of her and she was walking behind them and suddenly an over-speeding motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-9SW-6766 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") came out of nowhere and hit her, as a result, she sustained severe injuries including fracture in her right leg and injuries to her forehead.
Thereafter, crowd gathered and someone from the crowd called the police.
Police arrived on the spot and took her to Hindu Rao Hospital where she was admitted for medical treatment and her MLC bearing no. 3648/2021 was prepared.
PS Gulabi Bagh was registered by the police with respect to above accident.
R-1 is stated to be the driver, R-2 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
R-1 and R-2 were directed to file their Written Statements.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2025.08.21 10:08:49 +0530 heavy as that is required in a criminal case,
but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530,
which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs.
Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

sentences.text: As already discussed above, the petitioner examined herself as PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.

PW-1 has clearly and categorically stated that at the relevant date, time and place, she alongwith her two brothers Sh. Manish Pal and Sh. Nitesh Pal was travelling from Chandigarh to Delhi to visit her uncle's house and they were walking on footpath near Shastri Nagar Metro Station, heading towards Pratap Nagar Metro Station.

Her brothers were walking ahead of her and she was walking behind them and suddenly an over-speeding motorcycle i.e. offending vehicle came out of nowhere and hit her, as a result, she sustained severe injuries including fracture in her right leg and injuries to her forehead.
Thereafter, crowd gathered and someone from the crowd called the police.
Police arrived on the spot and took her to Hindu Rao Hospital where she was admitted for medical PANKAJ

SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.08.21 10:08:51 +0530 treatment and her MLC bearing no. 3648/2021 was prepared. PW-1 was not cross-examined on behalf of Respondents.
There is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW-1.

As such,
it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
Therefore, it has come out that petitioner Sunita Pal suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.

10. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC, 3/181 and 146/196 of M.V. Act in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of chargesheet, FIR, Site plan, MLC, Mechanical Inspection Report, arrest memo etc.
also corroborate the testimony of PW-1.
11.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Sunita Pal (I)(Fir288/2021/Gulabi ... vs Deepak @ Salu on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41125902/

In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in rash and PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.08.21 10:08:53 +0530 negligent manner in a high speed and hit the petitioner and petitioner got injured.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/
sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
13. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by her in the above accident.

14. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered injuries on her person on account of negligence and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
PANKAJ
by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards her treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.

The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
Sunita Pal (I)(Fir288/2021/Gulabi ... vs Deepak @ Salu on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41125902/
6 2025.08.21 10:08:57 +0530 only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on her earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
17.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.08.21 10:08:59 +0530 (i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.
The petitioner has placed on judicial file her original medical bills, which are Ex. PW-1/F(colly).
As per the said documents, petitioner has incurred expenses to the tune of Rs.935/-.
In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.935/- under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 19.
As per medical documents, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and is the case of FUC of # BB Rt leg and also sustained 18% permanent disability in relation to her right lower limb.

As per disability certificate no.2162 dated 21.05.2025 issued by Aruna Asaf Ali Govt. Hospital, Delhi and was found to have sustained 18% permanent physical impairment in relation to right lower limb.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which she actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as Sunita Pal (I)(Fir288/2021/Gulabi ... vs Deepak @ Salu on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41125902/
7 stated above, an effort PANKAJ Date:

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said period of her treatment and immobility.
Thus, she is awarded a total amount of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of studies 20.
In affidavit Ex. PW1/1, petitioner claims that she was 21 years old and she was unable to appear for her exams and her studies were disrupted.
Considering the nature of grievous injuries, a lump sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards loss of studies.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 21.
Petitioner claimed that she has become permanently disabled after the accident.

Admittedly,
petitioner has suffered 18% permanent physical impairment with respect to right lower limb.
Therefore, it is apposite to note that petitioner has become incapacitated to work following physical disability.

Due to injuries, she has become permanent disabled to the extent of 18% in the vital part of the body i.e. the leg due to which she is unable to sit and walk properly which has directly effected her vocation.
Since she is working, the said disability would be an impediment in her day to day working thereby diminishing her earning prospects.

In these PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.08.21 10:09:04 +0530 circumstances and in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be prudent to assess her functional disability to a extent of 18%.
Petitioner
claimed in her affidavit that she suffered loss of income.
However, she has not filed any documentary proof regarding her employment and earning.

In the absence of any corroborative material supporting the claim of the petitioner as to her employment or her monthly earnings, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Haryana as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Haryana at the relevant time).
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person as on 15.10.2021 in Haryana were Rs.9,803.24/-.
As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, she was 21 years.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her Sunita Pal (I)(Fir288/2021/Gulabi ... vs Deepak @ Salu on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41125902/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2025.08.21 10:08:49 +0530 heavy as that is required in a criminal case,
but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530,
which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs.
Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
As such,
it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
Therefore, it has come out that petitioner Sunita Pal suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/
sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion,
this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards her treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on her earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
17.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said period of her treatment and immobility.
Since she is working, the said disability would be an impediment in her day to day working thereby diminishing her earning prospects.
In these PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

In the absence of any corroborative material supporting the claim of the petitioner as to her employment or her monthly earnings, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Haryana as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Haryana at the relevant time).
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her Sunita Pal (I)(Fir288/2021/Gulabi ... vs Deepak @ Salu on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41125902/
